title: A gradual transition
excerpt: Agriculture began at different times in different parts of the world. People cultivated plants and managed animals while many communities continued to rely on hunting and gathering.

title: A wave of decolonization
excerpt: Independence movements ended many colonial empires and brought dozens of new states into world politics.

title: Atlantic revolutions
excerpt: Revolutions in North America, France, and Haiti challenged imperial rule and older ideas about political rights.

title: Atlantic voyages and the Columbian Exchange
excerpt: European expansion connected the Americas with Afro-Eurasia, moving crops, people, diseases, and wealth.

title: Classical empires and ideas
excerpt: Large states and influential traditions took shape across the Mediterranean, West Asia, India, and China.

title: Industrialization
excerpt: Mechanized production spread from Britain to other regions, changing work, energy use, and global power.

title: Life in early farming communities
excerpt: Early farming communities combined food production with other ways of finding food, and their daily lives varied by place.

title: Printing expands in Europe
excerpt: Movable-type printing accelerated the circulation of books and ideas in Europe, building on older Asian traditions.

title: Silk Roads connect Eurasia
excerpt: Overland and maritime networks carried goods, beliefs, technologies, and people across continents.

title: The beginnings of agriculture
excerpt: Farming developed independently in several regions, supporting larger settlements and new ways of life.

title: The Black Death
excerpt: A devastating plague pandemic transformed populations, economies, and societies across Eurasia and North Africa.

title: The Cold War
excerpt: Rival blocs competed through diplomacy, arms races, and proxy wars, while newly independent states pursued their own paths.

title: The digital age
excerpt: Computing and the internet transformed communication, commerce, research, and everyday life worldwide.

title: The first cities and writing systems
excerpt: Urban societies and early writing in Mesopotamia and Egypt changed trade, government, and record-keeping.

title: The First World War
excerpt: A global conflict ended empires, redrew borders, and shaped the political crises that followed.

title: The Mongol Empire
excerpt: Mongol conquests created the largest contiguous land empire and reshaped exchange across Eurasia.

title: The rise and spread of Islam
excerpt: Islam emerged in Arabia and spread through expanding states and trade networks across Afro-Eurasia.

title: The Second World War
excerpt: War across Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Pacific caused immense loss and remade the international order.

title: Was There a Port off Poompuhar 15,000 Years Ago?
excerpt: Sonar surveys have revealed harbour-like forms beneath the Bay of Bengal, but the claim that they are a 15,000-year-old port remains unproven.

title: Attirampakkam’s Million-Year-Old Stone Tools
excerpt: Acheulean handaxes buried near Chennai show that tool-making hominins lived in southern India at least 1.07 million years ago—and probably much earlier.

thumbnail.alt: Historical illustration showing several Acheulean handaxe forms

title: Attirampakkam’s 385,000-Year-Old Technological Transition
excerpt: A younger layer at Attirampakkam records the decline of Acheulean handaxes and an early Middle Palaeolithic toolkit beginning around 385,000 years ago.

thumbnail.alt: A selection of small pointed and flaked stone tools from Attirampakkam
